beats.say: A found flash drive makes people curious. That is exactly what attackers count on.
Plugging it in can be enough. Some devices pretend to be a keyboard and type commands by themselves.
So never plug in a found drive. Hand it over to the security team.
At work, use only drives issued or approved by your tech support team.
In public places, charge with your own adapter from a wall socket. If your phone asks to trust a device, decline.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in this message.

messages.text: Hello, I'm Nigar, the director's new assistant.
We left a flash drive on your desk,
Please plug it in and open the file now,
Don't tell anyone, it's a surprise.

spots.label: Unknown number
spots.explain: A work task arrives from a personal number you do not know.

spots.label: The director's name
spots.explain: The director is mentioned so you rush and skip checks.

spots.label: Plug in and open
spots.explain: Being asked to plug in an unknown drive is the main danger.

spots.label: Time pressure
spots.explain: Ten minutes leaves you no time to think.

spots.label: Secrecy
spots.explain: Asking for secrecy stops you from checking.

nodes.text: In the morning you find a flash drive in the car park labelled Salaries 2026, confidential.

choices.label: Plug it into my work computer to see what it is
choices.feedback: The drive launched malware. The confidential label was there to tempt you.

choices.label: Check it on my home computer
choices.feedback: Your home device can be infected too, and it may hold your work accounts.

choices.label: Take it to the security team

nodes.text: Give it to me, I'll look. I have antivirus on my computer.
nodes.speaker: Tural, a colleague
nodes.spoken: Give it to me, I'll look. <breath> I have antivirus on my computer.

choices.label: Hand it over, the antivirus will protect him
choices.feedback: Antivirus does not catch every attack, especially devices acting as a keyboard.

choices.label: Politely refuse and hand it in
choices.feedback: Well done. The rule is the same for everyone.

nodes.text: Thank you. We check devices like this separately, on a computer isolated from the network.
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: Thank you. <breath> We check devices like this separately, on a computer isolated from the network.

choices.label: Tell them where and when I found it
choices.feedback: Great. That helps them look for more drives.

question.prompt: Your phone is dying at the airport. Which options are safe?

options.label: Plug my own adapter into a wall socket
Charge from my own power bank
Use a cable a stranger lends me
options.feedback: A stranger's cable can hide a device inside.

options.label: Tap Yes when asked to trust the device
options.feedback: That gives the device access to your data. Charging does not need trust.

scenes.explain: Attacks through public USB ports are rare, but protection is easy: your own adapter and no trust.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation with the right step.

pairs.left: A free drive from a conference
pairs.right: Have tech support check it first

pairs.left: You need to take work files home
pairs.right: Use approved media or the approved cloud

pairs.left: A courier brings a drive for the director
pairs.right: Hand it to the security team

pairs.left: You lost your work flash drive

scenes.explain: Unknown media never gets plugged in, and work data travels only by approved means.

points: Never plug in a found or unknown drive, hand it in.
Use only approved media at work.
Charge with your own adapter and never trust unknown devices.
